I independently rebuilt Bloch matrices and checked the two exact trace/discriminant expressions at four parameter-time cases, plus normalized near-transition finite-difference slopes at z=−1,0,1; they approach the stated universal profile. Local Gram offdiagonal is ε²q versus correlator εq(aq²+b), generating ε² vs ε avoided-crossing widths; positive offdiagonal makes analytic finite-time G for every ε>0. Source Taylor expansions are compact-uniform with derivative because leading radicands are bounded away from zero when 0<b<a; ε=0 returns a cusp at t0. These analytic arguments, not finite sampling, cover all fixed a,b and bounded z.
